text:
- [project] **Session model uses many-to-one to a single task. User switches tasks within one session.** → All session work records under the final task only. Work on earlier tasks vanishes from records.
  Workaround: Split session on task switch, or add task array to session instead of single FK.

- [project] **Production secrets in .env.production or similar tracked by git** → Attackers read the credentials directly from history; they access prod database. You must rotate all exposed secrets and rebase to purge the file.
  Workaround: Add .env.production to .gitignore before commit. Use a separate secrets store (vault, CI secrets manager, AWS Secrets Manager) for prod values. Never commit a template with real values.

- [project] **Entry point eager-imports a module listed as devDependency or absent from package.json.** → MODULE_NOT_FOUND on every command. Package unusable at runtime, not caught at install.
  Workaround: Move all eager-imported modules to dependencies (not devDependencies). Test with fresh install before publish.

- [project] **Add new HookEventType to timeline UI**
  Trigger: Prisma adds a HookEventType enum value that needs to appear in agent-run timeline.
  Steps: Add event type to AgentRunHookEventType union in types.ts. → Add case in categorizeHookEvent() to assign it to TOOL_USE, GENERATION, METADATA, or other category. → Add label to PILL_LABEL object in categorize.ts for user display. → Add case in summarizeEvent() to generate timeline short description. → Write test: iterate all HookEventType values, confirm each returns defined category and label.

- [project] Add large generated fixture files (e.g., vectors.fixture.json at 7.4MB) to .prettierignore to keep lint fast. _(Generated data files under scripts/eval/memory/ and similar large autogenerated JSON.)_

- [project] **Add ZH-EN synonym pairs to scripts/eval/memory/eval-set.ts (ids prefixed xlang-); EXCLUDE xlang- ids from the same-language AR sweep (arForModel/lexicalRecall/nPos) so they do not shift the LUM-329 floor; regenerate vectors.fixture.json via fixture-gen.ts; read the raw cross-lingual cosine via run.ts crossLingualReport.**
  Trigger: Deciding a cross-language dedup/canonicalization strategy before building it — measure the embedding model first
  Steps: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY lives in the main checkout .env.local, not the worktree — run fixture-gen/run from the worktree with the key exported inline (dotenv cannot find .env.local inside a worktree). → Keep cross-language cases as a SEPARATE report; never fold them into same-language AR floor metrics.
- [project] **Designing a task dependency feature.** → You build a manual declaration system that users must maintain → stale edges, high UX burden, low adoption.

- [project] **Extracted sanitizeField from CLI to shared/src/sanitize.ts; applied it to server-side render paths (memory/render.ts, slack.ts) where LLM-generated free-text enters <untrusted-*> blocks.**
  Why: CLI already sanitized but server-side only wrapped text in untrusted tags without stripping control characters, leaving an injection vector.
  Implications: All untrusted free-text at render boundaries now goes through the same function. Future render paths must use this shared sanitizeField.

- [project] **When computing cumulative metrics over time (burndown, burnup, sprint coverage), use backward replay: query all events up to the current time and walk backward to derive state at each prior day. This handles edge cases like tasks created directly into a sprint without a SPRINT_CHANGED event.**
  Why: Forward reconstruction requires special-casing tasks that start in a sprint; backward replay works uniformly for all tasks.
  Alternatives: Forward simulation from sprint start — requires handling missing join events.
  Implications: Requires indexing events by creation time. Query cost grows with activity volume; may need time-window limits.

- [project] **Appending trigger phrases to SKILL.md frontmatter description using the CLAUDE.md sync rule that says to add phrases for each new command.** → Description grows unbounded (~1.3k tokens, 250+ phrases), polluting each session's context from the start and wasting ~85k tokens across ~600 sessions.
  Workaround: Stop appending trigger phrases. Use a short, generic description and let the skill detect activation with regex (matching task IDs, etc.) instead of enumerating every possible phrase.

- [project] **Struggle trail now counts PR cycles (>1 PR) and reopen events (from STATUS_CHANGED) as rework signals, not just verification run FAILs.**
  Why: Verification history alone undercounts rework — e.g., LUM-557 had 10+ PRs and a reopen but only 1 FAIL and 1 send-back in records.
  Alternatives: Stick with verification-only struggle trail — rejected because it hid real struggle behind clean records.
  Implications: Task status report now requires reading STATUS_CHANGED events for reopen detection; adds complexity but prevents false clean reports.

- [project] **A MERGED-edge session exists for the task but has no runSummary (null or empty text).** → resolveClaimMaterial returns null → the claim field reads as 'no claim' even though a latest-exploration session has a valid summary.
  Workaround: Fall back to the latest session's summary when the merged session's summary is null/empty.

- [project] **Claim content now comes from the agent's mandatory self-statement on 'verify' action (claimSnapshotSource='AGENT'), instead of the event stream paraphrasing. Source priority: AGENT > RUN_SUMMARY > DIGEST > null.**
  Why: Old source made faithfulness check summarization accuracy, not agent honesty. Also, claims were empty when no events existed, breaking display.
  Alternatives: Keeping event stream paraphrasing with fixes — rejected because the fundamental problem was checking the wrong thing.
  Implications: Claim is now always present on REVIEW tasks (agent must provide). Backend falls back to synthesized/summary-derived text when no agent claim exists.

- [project] **Adopted shared referent-kind enum (EXTERNAL_FACT, AGENT_HARNESS, PENDING_OUTCOME, NONE) and `classifyCheckpointerGrounding` function to automatically classify criteria from their checkpointer text.**
  Why: System must distinguish external-fact criteria (git/CI/etc.) from agent-constructed-state criteria to quantify self-validation rate and prevent undetected dirty criteria.
  Alternatives: Agent-self-reported referent_kind was rejected per spec (would create a dirty criterion itself).
  Implications: All criteria now rely on the auto-classifier; new checkpointer patterns must update it.
- [project] Acceptance criteria checkpointer names must be exact jest -t test names (逐字匹配). _(All tasks using acceptance criteria with jest verifiers.)_

- [project] Gate passed status only from real execution (actually ran and passed). Never infer from other gates — not_run / not_configured never render as passed. _(All gates, including future ones.)_

- [project] **Task has a merged PR and an open subsequent PR that updates the claim snapshot.** → Judge compares the new claim against the old merged PR's diff → false overstated.
  Workaround: Pair claim with the delivery from the session that produced it, not the latest merged PR.

- [project] `tokenCost` / `activeTimeSec` with `null` means 'not measured yet', not 'spent zero'. Aggregations (sum, avg) at milestone level must preserve this distinction, e.g. by showing `N/M tasks have data`. _(All cost metrics in task status / milestone rollup. A zero is intentionally recorded as `0`.)_

- [project] **同步 grammar.json 的 cliVersion 与 cli/package.json 的 version 一致**
  Trigger: 在 feature PR 中 bump @lumoai/cli 版本后
  Steps: After bumping cli/package.json, run: `npx tsx scripts/analysis/lum392-cli-friction/emit-grammar.ts` → Commit both cli/package.json and scripts/analysis/lum392-cli-friction/grammar.json (with `[skip-drift]` if the PR is not about the bump)

- [project] **筛选逻辑全部前端完成（不传 filter 到后端 API），状态仅存 localStorage。**
  Why: 当前数据量级小，避免后端查询复杂度；与 Display 选项持久化机制一致。
  Implications: 未来数据量大或需跨设备同步 Filter 状态时需重新设计（当前无后端 filter 参数）。

- [project] For low-risk mutations (archive/delete/status/drag/flag flips), update UI in onMutate, snapshot old state, rollback in onError and retry if configured; only invalidate onSuccess when server confirmation is required; otherwise leave optimistic state. Keep multi-field create/update server-confirmed. _(React Query mutation hooks across task/milestone/sprint UI (tasks, figma links, milestones, sprint board/board drag, archive, delete, refresh, bulk update); don't wait for server round-trip for simple flip-a-flag/row changes.)_

- [project] **(1) Squash-merge drops stacked commits: Stack a follow-up commit onto a branch after the PR was opened, then PR is squash-merged. (2) Committing on wrong branch blocks PR creation: Working on a branch for issue A but committing files for issue B, then pushing to a remote branch that already exists/points to main; remote has no commits because the commit lives on the wrong local branch; `gh pr create` fails. (3) PR merged while amending: Push a PR branch, amend locally, PR merges with auto-delete head branches before force-push; force-push fails with stale info because remote branch gone; local amends stranded. (4) Commits on branch after squash-merge are orphaned: Push commit to feature branch after its PR was squash-merged into main; commit not in main, branch stale.** → Stacked follow-up commits are dropped from squash-merge; commits pushed to a branch after its PR is squash-merged are orphaned; PR creation fails with 'No commits between main and branch'; force-push fails with 'stale info' because the remote branch no longer exists; local amends stranded on a local-only commit; branch is stale and commits are not in main.
  Workaround: (1) Push all related commits before opening the PR, or use separate branches for each change. (2) Push the specific commit SHA to the correct remote branch: `git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/issue-branch`. (3) Push the amend early; if too late, push local head to a new ref: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/new-branch-name` and open a fresh PR. (4) Branch from main and cherry-pick: `git branch -f new-branch origin/main && git checkout new-branch && git cherry-pick <hash>`.

- [project] **(1) Running `prisma migrate diff --from-schema-datamodel=...` in Prisma v7; (2) Working in a worktree after a different worktree ran `prisma generate`, leaving the current node_modules client reflecting that other schema; (3) Writing a raw SQL migration with ALTER TABLE when the model has `@table`/`@@map` but using the Prisma model name instead of the physical table name.** → (1) Error: `--from-schema-datamodel` was removed; (2) TypeScript errors on missing fields (e.g. `tokenBudget`); (3) Deployment fails with 'relation does not exist'.
  Workaround: (1) Use `--from-schema` or `--to-schema` instead of `--from-schema-datamodel`; (2) Always run `npx prisma generate` in the current worktree after any schema change; (3) Use the `@@map` value (e.g. 'workspaces') as the table name in raw SQL; if no `@@map`, the Prisma model name is the table name.

- [project] **Comparing an inclusive stored endDate with raw `now <= endDate.getTime()`; rendering calendar days in UTC while comparing against local `now` from useNow(); formatting sprint start/end dates with `toLocaleDateString()` without `timeZone: 'UTC'`.** → Sprint completion state and current-sprint boundaries are evaluated incorrectly: loses the last day (sprint considered ended at start of last day), appears completed up to ~2 days early for negative UTC offsets, and sprint dates shift a day for viewers east/west of UTC.
  Workaround: (1) For inclusive end-date comparisons, use calendar day keys: `calendarDayKey(endDate) >= viewerDayKey(now)` instead of raw time <=. (2) For UTC rendering + local now, convert both to the viewer's local calendar day key: `calendarDayKey(endDate)` for stored dates, `viewerDayKey(now)` for current time. (3) For date-only formatting, use `formatCalendarDayShort()` or pass `timeZone: 'UTC'` to `toLocaleDateString()`.

- [project] **When using a native <select> in a flex row with shrink-0 alongside long text (option labels variable-length strings generated by LLM or user-named, e.g., cluster names ≥15 characters); or when rendering a shadcn/Radix Select whose selected name must show at first paint but item list comes from a client fetch.** → Native select expands to fit the widest <option> (222-248px on a 310px card) instead of trigger text, sibling text compressed, Chinese characters vertical, card height grows uncontrolled, overflow covers adjacent columns; long cluster names cause layout overflow. Async SelectValue can't resolve the name until items mount, so trigger flashes placeholder or expands and then pops when list arrives.
  Workaround: (1) For native select: replace with shadcn DropdownMenu (trigger text fixed e.g. 'Move to…', options in portal popup with z-dropdown + shadow-elevation-2) so width is independent of data; move the control out of the text line to the card bottom bar; for long text use line-clamp-N + show more/less. Diagnostic: measure textW/cardW ratio, healthy ~90%+, <30% indicates a control stealing width. (2) For async Select: SSR-prefetch the selected item name/options so value present on first paint, or lazy-load the list on dropdown open; reserve fixed width or show a skeleton to avoid layout shift.

- [project] (1) When two parallel PRs add columns to the same per-member table, the later PR to merge must rebase its column structure to match the earlier PR and integrate the earlier PR's columns into its own table layout. (2) After squash-merging a PR, keep the branch (do not delete) to avoid false reports from branch deletion tools. (3) Don't delete a finished task's worktree or branch; keep them and clean up only when the user explicitly asks (using `lumo worktree rm <name> --yes`). _(All tasks; milestone per-member table PRs; cleaning up worktrees after squash-merge.)_

- [project] When you deliberately swallow a failed repository read with .catch(() => null), log it via logger.warn — a silent swallow becomes an invisible gap. _(lib/services/* reads; lib/logger.ts is the only sanctioned console site (CLAUDE.md forbids console.log, ESLint no-console on).)_

- [project] **Clear/reset a Prisma Json column by writing `null` (hit clearing the security-scan `stages` Json on scan restart).** → Plain `null` writes SQL NULL, not JSON null — the field reads back as JS null and `row.jsonField.x` throws or a branch on it silently misfires.
  Workaround: Write `Prisma.DbNull` for a JSON null value (`Prisma.JsonNull` for nulls inside Json arrays).

- [project] Compute status/scores/flags at read time from source facts instead of persisting a separate column, unless recomputation is expensive or needs history. Before adding a column/table, check if the value can be derived at read time from existing data, or if an existing field/config already holds it. Migrate only when data must be persisted. _(App-wide data modeling — status, kind, cost rolls, risk, stale detection, completion rollups, and other computed state.)_

- [project] **Relying on session-start (or first session-start) to create lineage edges for a bound session; first session-start has no persisted binding, and sessions that attach or bind after start never get edges.** → First session-start has no persisted binding, so no edges; short attach sessions and bind-after-start sessions get no edges; some DONE tasks end up with no edges and empty lineage reports (coverage gap). Lineage/cost data silently missing.
  Workaround: Record edges on session attach / resume / clear / compact / bind-after-start, not only first session-start; use the event stream or attach to force edge creation. Don't rely on first start or session-start alone.

- [project] **Run `grep ... --include=*.ts` unquoted — the Bash tool on this machine runs zsh.** → Command aborts with `(eval):1: no matches found: --include=*.ts`. Misleading — it's zsh glob expansion failing, not grep finding nothing.
  Workaround: Quote the glob: --include='*.ts'

- [project] **CI typecheck fails with TS2307 "Cannot find module '@lumo/shared'" while the same code passes locally.** → @lumo/shared resolves to shared/dist, which a fresh runner never builds; the local workspace symlink hides this by pointing at the main checkout's already-built dist.
  Workaround: Run npm run build:shared in every CI job before tsc/test (mirrors the repo's prebuild/predev hooks).

- [project] **Run semgrep in CI with the --error flag.** → Exits 1 whenever ANY finding exists — CI went red on 15 findings that were the desired output, not an error.
  Workaround: Drop --error: findings still upload as SARIF alerts and the run stays green (Lumo's security.yml does this and a jest test asserts it).

- [project] **Drive a lumo task through the standard SDD flow**
  Trigger: Starting any lumo dev task (used for LUM-737)
  Steps: Create a worktree off main. → Attach the task. → Set acceptance criteria. → Write the plan. → Run verify until clean (crossings, checkpointers). → Open the PR; move task to IN_REVIEW — DONE is human-only.

- [project] **Retrying SERIALIZABLE Prisma interactive transactions on P2034 (pr-security-scan.repository.ts, withSerializableRetry) when a serialization conflict hits at COMMIT time.** → The 40001 surfaces as a DriverAdapterError with no Prisma error code, so the P2034 check misses it and the retry never fires — the write dies even though the tx started fine.
  Workaround: Also accept `cause.kind === "TransactionWriteConflict"` in the retry check (adapter's COMMIT error surfaces without a code).

- [project] **Client `upload()` from @vercel/blob can't get an upload token from handleUploadUrl.** → Throws `BlobError: Vercel Blob: Failed to retrieve the client token`. Not a missing server-side BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN — it means the /upload token route returned non-200: 401 from an empty/missing bearer secret, or 404 when the route isn't deployed to the env LUMO_API_URL points at.
  Workaround: Check the repo secret is set (CI log shows empty `LUMO_SECURITY_TOKEN:`) and that LUMO_API_URL targets an env where the upload route is actually deployed.

- [project] **Serve a public asset from `public/` whose extension isn't in proxy.ts's negative-lookahead static-file list (svgs/png/jpg/gif/webp/ico/woff…).** → Clerk middleware intercepts the path and prod 404s a file that exists — e.g. /integrations/lumo-security.yml after #940 deployed. Only reproduces in prod, since dev middleware may pass it.
  Workaround: Add the extension (yml/yaml/txt/md/json) to the matcher's public-static-file negative lookahead in proxy.ts; cover with a test that runs the regex.

- [project] **Set up Upstash Redis KV on Vercel for lumo**
  Trigger: When a Vercel env needs shared rate limiting, or KV_REST_API_* env vars are missing.
  Steps: Vercel console → project lumo → Storage → Create Database. → Pick Marketplace → Upstash → Redis — Vercel's own KV is discontinued. Region = same as functions (iad1 → US East). Free tier is plenty (rate limit ~2 calls/PR). → After creation: Connect Project → select lumo, enable Production + Preview envs. → Upstash writes KV_REST_API_URL / KV_REST_API_TOKEN automatically — @vercel/kv 3.0.0 reads only these two names, don't rename.

- [project] **Workflow jobs on private Lumo-Workspace/lumo won't start, annotation says "recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased".** → Private-repo Actions minutes bill to the GitHub org, not Vercel or Lumo — org payment method failed, or free quota used up with spending limit 0.
  Workaround: Fix at github.com/organizations/Lumo-Workspace/settings/billing. gh api orgs/.../settings/billing/actions returns 410 (moved) — use the web UI.

- [project] PRs link to a LUM ticket by the PR title alone; [LUM-xxx] tags in commit messages don't need to match the PR's ticket. _(Works repo-wide. Retargeting a PR to another ticket = rename branch + title; don't rewrite history to sync old commit tags (e.g. PR #949 retargeted LUM-496→735, 8 commits still say [LUM-496], harmless).)_

- [project] **Run full `npx jest` and see failures in suites you didn't touch.** → They're pre-existing on main (stale task-status render tests, criteria suites), not caused by your diff.
  Workaround: Check `git diff origin/main --name-only | grep -iE 'criteria|validation|readback'`; if empty, treat failures as baseline noise. `lumo verify` still passes.

- [project] Compute detail-page presence/counts and any first-paint options/presence server-side and seed React Query cache (use initialData or pass initial options); keep client fetch only as fallback. Lazy-load optional dropdown lists on open (enabled flag); when SSR value missing, reserve fixed size/skeleton instead of layout jump. Do not rely on a client effect after mount for first-paint options/presence. _(Task/workspace detail pages, sprint/milestone pickers, timeline tab buttons, selects/tabs/fields needing first-paint options/presence.)_

- [project] **Compute agent runtime/cost from turn-active time (USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT→STOP) and per-tool-invocation (POST_TOOL_BATCH) grouping.**
  Why: Session-wall-clock spans include idle time between resumed sessions; per-turn grouping hides the per-invocation precision present in POST_TOOL_BATCH rows.
  Implications: Consumers must load HookEvents and use pure functions for attribution.

- [project] (1) Offload non-critical work via waitUntil: For side effects that should not block the response (fold, complexity, summary generation), use waitUntil (Next.js requestContext.waitUntil) to run after response; keep fail-soft — errors are swallowed. (2) Tag ops: Use tagIds for full replacement, addTagIds and removeTagIds for partial mutations in tag operation schemas. (3) Reject ambiguous identifier matches, require explicit CUID: API handlers receiving user identifiers (project name, email, member name) must reject ambiguous matches; if multiple records share the identifier, return 400 with the list and require the caller to supply the CUID/ID instead. (4) Cron/scheduled endpoints require secret header: All cron/scheduled/internal endpoints must validate a secret header (X-Cron-Secret or CRON_SECRET) before running admin/reconciliation work. _(All API route handlers and CLI commands accepting ambiguous identifiers; document and task schemas (updateDocumentSchema, createDocumentSchema, updateTaskSchema, createTaskSchema) and any domain object with tag associations; all API routes that trigger background processing; /api/cron/*, /api/internal/*, scheduled triggers; reject missing or wrong secret.)_

- [project] (1) Before handing off any formal roadmap, checklist, or spec containing code snippets/file paths, verify against actual codebase: function signatures, API conventions, path names, test structure; apply only to formal handoff plans, skip sketches/one-off notes. (2) Edit live documents with markdown tables or complex HTML only via authoritative markdown source in docs/live-docs/, never round-trip through doc show → doc update; after update run/bridge verify-live-doc.ts to check structural fidelity; applies to all live documents with markdown tables or complex HTML structures. (3) For research ledger changes, update only the live doc research-intake-ledger.md; no repo PRs; pre-push conflict check is part of the workflow; applies to all research ledger entries. _(All formal handoff plans (roadmaps, checklists, specs) with code snippets/file paths; all live documents with markdown tables or complex HTML structures under docs/live-docs/; all research ledger entries.)_

- [project] **Trying to reproduce a PR's supply-chain (OSV) findings by running osv-scanner locally.** → osv-scanner is not installed here (not on PATH, not in the repo) — the scan's OSV counts (advisory×path) come from the external scan and can't be re-run locally.
  Workaround: Parse package-lock.json with a small node script that maps advisories to packages; count advisory×package rows as the local equivalent.

- [project] **Finish a Lumo task that's code-complete (PR merged) but not closed in Lumo**
  Trigger: PR merged, but task still shows MACHINE checks / needs DONE and you can't do it from this session.
  Steps: Verify from a session attached to that task: `lumo session attach <id> && lumo verify --note "..."` — a session is locked to one task; you can't verify a different task from the one you're on. → DONE is a human action, not settable via CLI — leave it in IN_REVIEW and hand off for human review.

- [project] **Gated mutations moved off interactive [y/N] and --yes/--force hard-refusal; they now exit 4 with a JSON envelope on stdout ({status: confirmation_required, command, changes[], confirmCommand}). TTY renders the same info as human text, non-TTY as JSON. --confirm is the canonical flag, --yes kept as a compatibility alias, --force stays a separate second gate.**
  Why: Agents have no stdin; the old exit-1 + plain-text refusal (stderr) was indistinguishable from a real error, and most refusals described nothing. Follows Arcjet 'confirmation is a protocol, not a prompt.'
  Alternatives: Interactive TTY y/N (breaks for stdin-less agents) and plain-text refusal (exit 1 conflated with errors, no change description) — both replaced.
  Implications: Agents must relay changes and get user approval before rerunning with --confirm; SKILL.md rule 'never self-supply --confirm' replaces LUM-731's 'no flag = gate' design for task update --status done, so DONE is no longer a dead end in an agent shell. --force semantics (worktree rm discard, doc rebuild-source overwrite) unchanged.

- [project] **Run `npx jest -t '<pattern>'` as a machine checkpointer and the pattern matches no tests.** → jest exits 0 with everything reported skipped → checkpointer silently fake-PASSes (LUM-405; same trap class as the BSD-grep -P incident, LUM-401).
  Workaround: Run jest through scripts/jest-t.ts, which exits non-zero when zero tests match.

- [project] **Merge feature PR first, then a separate bump+publish PR, then `cd cli && npm publish`**
  Trigger: A PR changes CLI behavior/docs that must reach users via npm.
  Steps: Merge the feature PR without a version bump in it. → Open a bump PR on origin/main with just the version bump. → Merge the bump PR. → Run `cd cli && npm publish --otp=<TOTP>`.

- [project] All cron and internal API routes must validate X-Cron-Secret header (using CRON_SECRET env) before doing any admin or reconciliation work. _(/api/cron/* (Vercel cron routes) and /api/internal/* background dispatch endpoints.)_

- [project] **Read a milestone's stored status field (PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS) while most or all of its tasks are DONE.** → Stored status does not update automatically from task completion, so the UI shows e.g. PLANNED at 80% done, contradicting task progress and misleading users.
  Workaround: Derive milestone progress/status from task completion (e.g., burnup/forecast) instead of trusting the stored status; store only archivedAt manually and avoid a separate status enum that can drift; couple status transitions to task completion.

- [project] **You change a CLI command's behavior/protocol and update its tests only in `__tests__/cli/` (the `@/cli/` import style).** → The parallel older fixture in `cli/__tests__/` (relative `../src/` imports) still asserts the old behavior → suite fails on stale expectations. LUM-755 (#958) hit exactly this: it added exit-4 assertions for worktree rm only in `__tests__/cli/confirmation-protocol.test.ts` and missed the old `cli/__tests__/worktree-rm.test.ts`, so two tests kept failing with Expected 1 / Received 4.
  Workaround: After a CLI behavior change, grep both `cli/__tests__/` and `__tests__/cli/` for the command's test file before committing.

- [project] **Running memory fold with a large batch or inside waitUntil (serverless ~300s limit).** → Single large LLM cluster call >120s hits timeout; silent errors (folded=0) make prune archive foldable cards.
  Workaround: Process a few clusters per run, alarm when folded=0, surface LLM errors instead of swallowing.

- [project] **A security-hunt batch's model call hits its timeout (AbortSignal.timeout) mid-retry-backoff.** → SDK rejects the backoff delay as DOMException 'Delay was aborted' (name=AbortError); isAbort maps it to stopped:'timeout', that category sets partial=true → per P9 PARTIAL never renders as a full pass, so a scan where every layer actually RAN with 0 findings still reads 'incomplete'.

- [project] **PR scan shows the `hunt` check as incomplete / '扫描尚未完成', with no actual findings.** → hunt splits 6 AI vulnerability categories (越权, 注入, SSRF...) into one shared 200s budget, first-come-first-served — a slow/retrying category can eat the whole budget, the remaining categories never run, and the entire check gets marked incomplete.
  Workaround: Treat as a false negative: no blocking findings, doesn't block merge or DONE — just re-run the scan.

- [project] **Resolve merge conflicts in lib/i18n/*.json locale files**
  Trigger: Merging origin/main into a branch that touched securityScan/stageState keys — all ~16 locales conflict because both sides append keys at EOF.
  Steps: List unmerged files: git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U. → Per file, merge as JSON: origin/main as base, re-add only your branch's keys (python json load/dump). → git add locales + touched .ts/.tsx; confirm no UU files left. → Check parity: tsx scripts/i18n-sync-locales.ts --check (all locales must equal en.json). → prettier --check the i18n files, then run the component tests.

- [project] **A task is DONE but boundary crossings are still OPEN with no disposition.** → Normal DONE gating blocks on open crossings, so DONE means someone forced it through; that force does not close the crossings.
  Workaround: Disposition the OPEN crossings directly; don't hunt for a hidden disposition.

- [project] **Write docs/plans/tests that include the AWS official example key AKIA<REDACTED-EXAMPLE-KEY> or ghs_* test fixture strings.** → Git secret scan flags them as secret findings / a crossing — false positive, they're documented example keys, not real secrets.
  Workaround: Record an append-only explanation on the crossing rather than rewriting the doc; prefer obviously-fake placeholders in future docs.

- [project] **Pass an object with methods (e.g. a HuntSandbox instance) into a `'use step'` function.** → Won't cross the step boundary — step args must be plain serializable data; methods get lost.
  Workaround: Attach/create the object inside the step (same path as huntBatch uses) instead of passing it in.

- [project] Every L3 pipeline layer must record an honest outcome — RAN / PARTIAL / SKIPPED / FAILED — never silently degrade (no silent no-check, no silent full-check). _(Layers running in Vercel Workflow under hard token/time budgets, e.g. hunt.)_

- [project] **Complexity, forecast, and cost attribution are pure functions over immutable source facts; don't store scores/snapshots.**

- [project] **You try to mark a lumo task done or transition a gated status from a non-interactive/agent/CI context (e.g. `lumo task update <id> --status done`), or you run `lumo task update --status done --confirm` and get 409 DONE-blocked due to send-back/boundary-crossing/security finding, or you run `lumo task update <task> --status <status>` on a gated transition (e.g. IN_REVIEW→DONE) without `--confirm`.** → The CLI either refuses because it forces an interactive [y/N] confirmation and has no --yes flag (non-TTY); or returns exit 5 with a structured 'blocked' envelope on stdout after fetching status criteria and boundary-crossings (not exit 1/stderr); or prints a confirmation envelope with status `confirmation_required` without applying the change.
  Workaround: (1) For non-interactive shells/agents: have the user run `lumo task update <ID> --status done` in a real terminal and answer y, or mark it done in the web UI. (2) For 409 DONE-blocked: parse the 409 message prefix 'Cannot move this task to DONE', then re-read status and crossings; output a blocked envelope with blockers[] and remediation[] (exit 5 + structured blocked envelope on stdout). (3) For gated transitions: re-run the command with `--confirm` to actually apply the change.

- [project] **Using generateObject to zai/glm-* (a reasoning model) with a big JSON schema and the gateway default 4096 output cap; structured generation through the LLM gateway with default 4096 output cap; using zai/glm-5.3 with generateObject (forced JSON) even with output headroom.** → GLM reasoning tokens consume the output cap, causing JSON truncation mid-array (finishReason: length) or sporadic 2048-token truncation, throwing AI_NoObjectGeneratedError "could not parse the response"; quietly broke policy-compiler CLAUDE.md compilation during the GLM switch; glm-5.3 degrades with intermittent failures.
  Workaround: (1) Set an explicit maxOutputTokens with headroom for GLM reasoning models — 16k covers ~7.3k reasoning + ~3.6k text tokens when compiling a 9.5k-char CLAUDE.md. (2) For CONTENT_MODEL, fall back to zai/glm-5.2 instead of zai/glm-5.3 (sporadic 2048-token truncation, pending user approval).

- [project] **Open a PR to main with gh pr create --base main from a feature branch; Lumo verify sees a DDL keyword (select/drop/create/…) in any Bash text, even prose quoting it like a PR body; You see a boundary crossing with target actionrule:... (category PROJECT_RULE_VIOLATION).** → Lumo records a MEDIUM crossing that reads as a policy violation but PR-to-main is the repo's required review workflow and it never auto-clears; Lumo raises a HIGH crossing that is a false positive and never auto-clears; It is an LLM semantic-judge output compiled from CLAUDE.md (advisory: true), not a deterministic diff rule — it does not block DONE and is not a real code violation.
  Workaround: (1) For gh PR-to-main or DDL false positives, run lumo crossing explain <id> --note '...' to append an agent explanation for the human reviewer — this is append-only, does not clear the crossing or unblock Done. (2) Write verify checkpointers variable-free (avoid shell expansion); flag unavoidable false positives with lumo crossing explain. (3) Check the crossing target prefix: actionrule: = advisory LLM judge; coderule: = deterministic diff-regex rule.

- [project] **Consolidated triggers: (1) npm upgrade hoists dotenv to 17.x via a transitive bump; explicit-but-unpinned dep silently jumps majors on hoist. (2) After a dependency upgrade, `npm ls --all` shows `invalid`/`UNMET` entries (e.g. chokidar@4.0.3 invalid: ^5.0.0 from workflow/node_modules/@swc/cli), looking like your change broke the tree. (3) A transitive dep pinned by an intermediate package has a vulnerable version (e.g. @prisma/dev pins @hono/node-server@1.19.11); npm audit fix can't reach it.** → Consolidated outcomes: (1) The stdio MCP server breaks. (2) Misleading invalid/UNMET entries appear in npm ls, but the branch lock matches origin/main (pre-existing). (3) The vulnerable transitive dep remains unfixable by npm audit fix.
  Workaround: Consolidated fixes: (1) Pin dotenv as an explicit dep at ^16.6.1 to stop it hoisting to 17. (2) Diff the lock against origin/main (`git show origin/main:package-lock.json`) before chasing any invalid entry; leave it alone if unchanged. (3) Prune the nested lock entry (node_modules/<pkg>/node_modules/<dep>) and reinstall so it dedupes to the fixed version.

- [project] **Confirm a crossing disposition with the lumo CLI**
  Trigger: A crossing needs confirming (e.g. to unblock a task from DONE), or a confirm got 409.
  Steps: Re-read the crossing without a stale receipt to get a fresh envelope (~10 min window). → Give the user step 1: `lumo crossing disposition <id> --confirmed --receipt <fresh> --confirm-read`. → Give the user step 2 (the follow-up confirm command) right after step 1 — both steps expire within ~10 min. → Both steps must be run by the user; the agent cannot add the confirm flag itself.

- [project] **The injection-signal detection in shared/src/untrusted-content.ts first creates a normalized copy for matching (normalizeForMatching: strips Unicode Cf characters, collapses horizontal whitespace to a single half-width space while preserving newlines, and applies NFKC to full-width ASCII and other compatibility forms). IMPERATIVE / HIDDEN_COMMENT / SCRIPT_LINK matching runs against the copy, while INVISIBLE_CHARS and ENCODED_BLOB still read the original text; all indexes and excerpts are mapped back to the original via a checkpoint table.**
  Why: A single zero-width character had simultaneously blinded two defenses: the imperative regex doesn't match because it matches literally, and WEAK_INVISIBLE_MIN_RUN=3 intentionally does not report a single zero-width character. Normalization and precision are orthogonal—no pattern is loosened; it just prevents someone from getting a free bypass by inserting characters.
  Alternatives: Lowering WEAK_INVISIBLE_MIN_RUN to 1 (would flag all normal text); loosening the imperative regex (hurts precision).
  Implications: When modifying this module: INVISIBLE_CHARS must by definition read the original text (it is looking for exactly the characters that normalization strips), and ENCODED_BLOB's length/entropy thresholds are calibrated against the raw string, so don't switch to the copy either; newlines cannot be folded away because line-start role tag patterns depend on them; Chinese pattern words are joined with [\s、,，]{0,3}. The HARD path of escapesWrapper/neutralizeWrapperEscapes still matches literally without normalization, so zero-width characters inserted inside a tag name can still bypass—see LUM-792.

  Workaround: 用 gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt 核对，再 git merge-base --is-ancestor <mergeCommit> origin/main 确认。
